newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fletcher Energy says to develop Brunei field.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher Energy says to develop Brunei field.

text.p: Fletcher Energy Ltd and its partners said on Thursday that they had decided to proceed with development of the Maharaja Lela gas and condensate field, offshore from Brunei Darussalam.
The total development cost through to first production in January 1999 is US$230 millon.
Fletcher owns 35 percent and other shareholders included Elf Aquitaine (37.5 poercent), Bruneian company JASRA (22.5 percent and other Bruneian interests (5 percent).

Chief Executive of Fletcher Challenge Energy, Michael Andrews said the decision to proceed with development of the field follows the drilling of the Maharaja Lela 3 appraisal well earlier this year which encountered hydrocarbons in a number of reservoir sequences and produced 29 million standard cubic feet (mmscf) of gas and 444 barrels of condensate per day on test.
"This well confirmed joint venture's view that the field contained sufficient deliverable reserves to warrant development," Andrews said.
"We have concluded agreements for the processing and sale of gas and liquids from the field, enabling us to proceed with the development."
Andrews said the Maharaja Lela was typical of Bruneian fields in that it contained a relatively large number of hydrocarbon accumulations.

"This makes it relatively hard to assess the size of the field, however proven reserves have been assessed at 90 million barrels of oil equivalent (mmboe). Proven and probable reserves are 140 mmboe, probable and possible reserves are assessed at 250 mmboe."
A heads of agreement has been negotiated between the Maharaja Lela joint venture and Brunei LNG Sdn Bhd, under which the joint venture will deliver approximately 72 mmscf per day thereafter.
The decision to proceed with the project is based on proven reserves only, and the development is financially viable on this basis," Andrews said.
The heads of agreement incorporates a pricing formula which effectively links the price for the gas to oil prices in Japan. The final gas sales agreement will be signed early 1997.
